utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen, does the OTP have access to these archives?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We would have to make requests for assistance -- for assistance, I believe, as we normally do with access to archives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this not something that ought to have been invaded and investigated by the OTP if they had the authority, which seems to be fairly easy to get, to do it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, we are trying to obtain access to many different archives in different places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, is this one or are the KLA archives archives that you've tried to get access to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I would have to inquire. I don't know. I haven't seen -- well, yeah -- no, I would have to inquire to be able to answer your question correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The documents that you found that -- if I understand you were all of the documents that you could find, you've told us you turned over to the OTP office in Pristina. True?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And since you have been here at the Tribunal preparing for your testimony here, have you seen all the documents that you turned over to the Tribunal at the Pristina office?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those that were shown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So do you recall turning over other documents to the Pristina office that you haven't seen here?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many documents that I've submitted, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately when you turned these documents over to the OTP office in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was before I came here to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, that's fairly obvious. That doesn't help me very much. Can you give me something like a date that you might have done that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was it a year ago? Two years ago?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that long ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How long ago? Just give me your best guess. I don't know why you're playing with me about this. About how long ago was it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Perhaps two or three weeks before I travelled to here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ackerman, I think we should interrupt there for the evening. If you haven't already done so, then I suggest that you have at least a brief exchange with Mr. Marcussen to see if your knowledge of this can be advanced that way. That doesn't prevent you from continuing the cross-examination, but it might help you to focus it. And I'm not blaming you for that but it might help you to focus it better if --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have had some exchange by e-mail, and Mr. Marcussen has advised me that he has -- and I'm convinced that this is the case, that he's supplied me with every document that they have. The mystery that exists now is on the 31st of October we were given an e-mail from the Prosecutor's office saying, Here are a bunch of documents that the witness brought with him that we haven't seen before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And obviously they were turned over to their office in Pristina apparently sometime much before that. I don't know. This is a mystery to me and I don't -- I'm not making an accusation, but I sure am missing some information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But do you reckon that you've got the 85 to a hundred documents that were handed in at Pristina or have you had something less than that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's nowhere near 85 or a hundred documents. It's maybe 30 or 40 pages at best I would think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I suggest you have another exploratory discussion with Mr. Marcussen, rather than by e-mail, face-to-face, and see if you can't get a bit closer to the situation before continuing with the cross tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Maybe -- I cannot scroll back right now in the transcript, but it's 85 or a hundred pages, not documents, just to put that on the record, and I will meet with Mr. Ackerman afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Mr. Zyrapi, we have to interrupt again, I'm afraid, until tomorrow. But tomorrow you will have our attention from the start of the proceedings, which will be at 2.15. Meanwhile, I remind you of what I said before: Please don't discuss the evidence with anybody at all. And we'll see you again at 2.15 tomorrow. Please now leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 9th day of November, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
